question: WN4303 SFO-DEN on 2026-01-03 left 362 minutes late, and BTS blames 338 of that on a late inbound aircraft. Which inbound was it, and how far back can you trace the delay?

content.text: I'll start by pulling that flight and its rotation context.

input.sql: SELECT * FROM flights WHERE flight_number='4303' AND flight_date='2026-01-03' AND origin='SFO'
SELECT * FROM next_leg WHERE to_flight_id LIKE '2026-01-03|WN|4303|SFO|DEN%' OR from_flight_id LIKE '2026-01-03|WN|4303|SFO|DEN%'

content.text: Now tracing the tail back through the day.

input.sql: SELECT flight_id, origin, destination, sched_dep_utc, actual_dep_utc, sched_arr_utc, actual_arr_utc, dep_delay_minutes, arr_delay_minutes, sched_block_minutes, delay_carrier, delay_weather, delay_nas, delay_late_aircraft, status FROM flights WHERE tail_number='N8747Q' AND sched_dep_utc BETWEEN '2026-01-02 00:00:00+00' AND '2026-01-04 12:00:00+00' ORDER BY sched_dep_utc
SELECT * FROM next_leg WHERE tail_number='N8747Q' ORDER BY to_flight_id

content.text: Checking the break in the rotation upstream, the downstream leg, and the network context at PHX/SFO that evening.

input.sql: SELECT flight_id, origin, destination, sched_dep_utc, actual_dep_utc, dep_delay_minutes, arr_delay_minutes, delay_carrier, delay_nas, delay_late_aircraft FROM flights WHERE flight_id IN ('2026-01-04|WN|1554|DEN|PDX|0705','2026-01-04|WN|1554|PDX|SMF|0950','2026-01-04|WN|2770|SMF|PHX|1200')

SELECT origin, count(*) n, sum(CASE WHEN dep_delay_minutes>=60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) big, round(avg(dep_delay_minutes),1) avg_dep, sum(delay_nas) nas FROM flights WHERE origin IN ('PHX','SFO') AND sched_dep_utc BETWEEN '2026-01-03 20:00:00+00' AND '2026-01-04 08:00:00+00' GROUP BY origin

content.text: Let me look at the SFO station picture and other SFO-bound legs that evening.

input.sql: SELECT flight_id, tail_number, origin, sched_dep_utc, dep_delay_minutes, arr_delay_minutes, delay_carrier, delay_weather, delay_nas, delay_late_aircraft, status FROM flights WHERE destination='SFO' AND sched_arr_utc BETWEEN '2026-01-03 20:00:00+00' AND '2026-01-04 10:00:00+00' ORDER BY sched_arr_utc

content.text:
**The inbound was WN4124 PHX–SFO, tail N8747Q** (`2026-01-03|WN|4124|PHX|SFO|1840`). It was scheduled into SFO at 03:45Z and got in at 09:42Z — 357 minutes late. WN4303 (`2026-01-03|WN|4303|SFO|DEN|2025`) then turned in 45 minutes against a 40-minute scheduled turn and pushed at 10:27Z, +362. So essentially all of the 338 late-aircraft minutes are real: the aircraft simply wasn't in SFO, and the station added only ~5 minutes over a minimum turn (BTS coded 3 carrier minutes).

Walking N8747Q backwards, the chain runs four legs:

| Leg | Dep delay | Arr delay | Attribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| WN4686 COS–DEN (sched 23:10Z) | +100 | +90 | 28 carrier, 62 late aircraft |
| WN2601 DEN–PHX (sched 00:45Z) | +84 | +82 | 82 late aircraft |
| WN4124 PHX–SFO (sched 01:40Z) | +343 | +357 | 348 NAS, 9 late aircraft |
| WN4303 SFO–DEN (sched 04:25Z) | +362 | +341 | 338 late aircraft, 3 carrier |

Two things to flag about that trace.

**The big jump at PHX is not really inbound propagation — it's SFO flow control.** The delay grew from 82 to 343 minutes at PHX, and BTS put 348 of it on NAS. That is consistent with everything else arriving into SFO that evening: of 17 WN arrivals scheduled into SFO between 20:00Z Jan 3 and 10:00Z Jan 4, the NAS-coded ones include WN3665 STL–SFO (+294 dep, 304 NAS), WN2985 LAX–SFO (+205, 221 NAS), WN4250 SAN–SFO (+242, 220 NAS), WN3403 LAX–SFO (+190, 186 NAS), WN744 DEN–SFO (+177, 178 NAS) and WN3133 LAS–SFO (+155, 155 NAS). Every one of the 11 WN departures out of SFO in that window was in turn late-aircraft coded, up to WN1549 SFO–LAX at +324 (296 late aircraft) and WN4298 SFO–PHX at +229 (224 late aircraft). WN4303 is one station-wide event, not an isolated tail problem.

That said, the aircraft was also genuinely unavailable: WN2601 didn't put N8747Q on the ground in PHX until 04:12Z, 152 minutes after WN4124's 01:40Z scheduled departure. So at least 152 of WN4124's 343 minutes were aircraft-availability regardless of the NAS coding; the remaining ~191 minutes were spent sitting in PHX after the aircraft arrived. Note also that `chain_breaks` flags this pair as an **impossible_turn** (gap −70 minutes): WN4124 was scheduled to leave PHX 70 minutes *before* WN2601 was scheduled to arrive. That scheduled pairing is broken in the extract regardless of the delay, and I can't tell from this data whether it reflects a planned tail swap or a data artifact.

**The trace stops at COS.** WN4686 COS–DEN carries 62 late-aircraft minutes, but there is no linking leg into COS for this tail. The previous recorded flight for N8747Q is WN2343 AUS–MSY, arriving MSY 06:02Z on Jan 3, a 1,025-minute station discontinuity. Whatever made the aircraft 62 minutes late out of COS is outside this extract — you'd need the ferry/positioning leg or the actual inbound to COS to close that gap.

**Downstream, the cascade dies at DEN.** WN4303 arrived DEN at 12:31Z; the next leg, WN1554 DEN–PDX (`2026-01-04|WN|1554|DEN|PDX|0705`), was scheduled out at 14:05Z, giving 93 minutes of actual ground against a 40-minute 5th-percentile DEN turn (1,506 observed turns). It departed 14:04Z, one minute early, and arrived PDX 11 early. The overnight buffer absorbed all 341 minutes.
